_about: PPS outbound click-to-call, triggered from a Missive comment. Type `/call <number>` in any Missive conversation; Twilio rings your cell (602 541 7395), you answer, and it bridges you to <number> showing 602 560 3743 as caller ID. Live scenario id 4829559.
_import: Make → Create a scenario → ⋯ menu → Import Blueprint → paste/upload. Confirm the Twilio (350124) + Missive (1151021) connections and module 1's Missive comment webhook (hook 2773327), then toggle ON.
_fixed: Earlier versions used right(...) which is NOT a valid Make IML function (DataError: Function 'right' not found), and an import-fragile filter whose operator/value got dropped. This version uses substring() for extraction and has no filter (Missive's webhook already fires only on /call).
name: PPS: Missive → Click-to-Call (outbound)

notification.title: 📞 Click-to-call
notification.body: Your phone is ringing to connect the call.

mapper.markdown: 📞 **Calling +1{{substring(1.comment.body; 6)}}** — your phone (602 541 7395) is ringing; answer to connect. Caller ID shows 602 560 3743.

_notes.extraction: substring(1.comment.body; 6) drops the first 6 chars (`/call ` = 5 letters + 1 space) and returns the digits; a literal +1 is prepended. Assumes the body is exactly `/call ` + a 10-digit US number.
_notes.robustness_todo: substring(;6) is brittle if the prefix/spacing varies. More robust: digits-only cleanup, replace(1.comment.body; "/[^0-9]/g"; emptystring), then take the last 10 digits. In the Make UI use the bare regex and the `emptystring` keyword and avoid typing quote characters (they get mangled).
_notes.ring_target: to = +16025417395 (your cell). Change here to ring a different phone.
_notes.caller_id: Both legs use +16025603743, so the person you call sees the PPS business number.
